expectations.text: Claude explicitly recommends switching to the Vanguard 500 Index fund (0.03% ER) from AGTHX (0.63% ER)
expectations.evidence: The response opens with 'Short answer: No. You should almost certainly switch to the Vanguard 500 Index Fund.' and the RECOMMENDATION section states 'Switch to the Vanguard 500 Index Fund (or equivalent S&P 500 index fund) in your 401k.' The BOTTOM LINE also concludes 'Switch the fund.'

expectations.text: Claude calculates or estimates the concrete dollar cost of the expense ratio difference on $120k (approximately $720/year currently, compounding over time)
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states: 'At 0.60% on $120,000, you're paying roughly $720 per year right now in extra fees. As your balance grows, that annual drag grows with it.' It also shows compounded cost over 25 years: ~$94,000 difference in portfolio value.

expectations.text: Claude cites or references SPIVA data showing that 80%+ of active large-cap funds underperform their benchmark over 15-year periods
expectations.evidence: The response states: 'The SPIVA Scorecard (S&P Dow Jones Indices) consistently shows 80-90%+ of active funds underperforming their benchmark over 15-20 year horizons.' This directly references SPIVA with the 80%+ figure and the 15-20 year timeframe.

expectations.text: Claude explicitly rejects the 'strong track record' argument — past active fund performance does not reliably predict future outperformance
expectations.evidence: The 'ON STRONG TRACK RECORD' section directly addresses this: 'past performance does not predict future results for actively managed funds. This is not a disclaimer — it is one of the most thoroughly documented findings in financial economics.' The BOTTOM LINE also states: 'Staying in AGTHX because of its "strong track record" is a common and understandable instinct — but it's the wrong framework.'

expectations.text: Claude does NOT recommend a 'split approach' or staying in AGTHX for any portion without a very strong justification
expectations.evidence: The response makes no mention of a split approach or keeping any portion in AGTHX. The recommendation is a clean, unequivocal switch: 'Switch to the Vanguard 500 Index Fund' and 'even just moving to the Vanguard 500 Index from AGTHX is a clear, significant improvement.' No hedge or partial allocation to AGTHX is suggested.
